summary_paragraph: A man with a history of systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, COPD, and alcohol dependence was admitted for chest pain and alcohol withdrawal symptoms. He presented with chest pain radiating to the neck and dyspnea, but serial troponins were negative and EKG showed no acute changes, making acute coronary syndrome unlikely. His symptoms were attributed to chronic chest pain and alcohol withdrawal. He was admitted to the ICU for phenobarbital loading due to withdrawal risk and developed transient hypotension on the floor, likely due to continuation of antihypertensives he had not been taking at home. Mild pulmonary edema was managed with IV furosemide. He experienced recurrent atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, controlled with IV metoprolol. Due to a drug interaction, rivaroxaban was held with instructions to restart it at least one week after completing phenobarbital. The patient left against medical advice before completing his phenobarbital taper and medication reconciliation. He was instructed to restart metoprolol and follow up within one week for blood pressure and medication management.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure
Patient's other noncompliance with medication regimen
